metadata.title: A finite volume scheme for convection-diffusion equations with nonlinear diffusion derived from the Scharfetter-Gummel scheme

extraction_notes.note: The convergence-order evidence is two tables of errors and orders; they are not nodes, and their content is summarized by the numerical claim that cites them.
The motivation subsection's figure-based comparisons of upwind, Scharfetter-Gummel and nonlinear upwind fluxes are not extracted sentence by sentence; only the concluding remark is a node.
The \textbf{Estimate of ...} headings in these proofs are author labels but latex_facts detected only 'Conclusion.'; every heading was treated as a label starting a step.
The remark states an assertion and proves it ('Indeed, ...'); kept as remark with a nested claim and nested prose proof rather than retyping the remark.
The PDE initial-boundary value problem is typed problem; definition was the alternative.

The conclusion refers to 'the continuous framework (\ref{H})' for the energy estimate, but label H is the primitive H; the estimate meant is (inegentropie). The automatic \ref edge from H is kept and an edge from the estimate added.

nodes.statement: We supplement these equations with initial conditions $N_{0}(x)$ and $P_{0}(x)$ and physically motivated boundary conditions: the boundary $\Gamma=\partial \Omega$ is split into two parts $\Gamma=\Gamma^{D} \cup \Gamma^{N}$ and the boundary conditions are Dirichlet boundary conditions $ \overline{N}$, $ \overline{P}$ and $ \overline{V}$ on ohmic contacts $\Gamma^{D}$ and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions on $r(N)$, $r(P)$ and $V$ on insulating boundary segments $\Gamma^{N}$.

nodes.name: Convergence to thermal equilibrium for the drift-diffusion model
nodes.statement: The large time behavior of the solutions to the nonlinear drift-diffusion model (\ref{DD}) has been studied by A. Jüngel in \cite{Juengel1995a}. It is proved that the solution to the transient system converges to a solution of the thermal equilibrium state as $t \rightarrow \infty$ if the Dirichlet boundary conditions are in thermal equilibrium.
assumptions: if the Dirichlet boundary conditions are in thermal equilibrium
conclusions: the solution to the transient system converges to a solution of the thermal equilibrium state as $t \rightarrow \infty$

nodes.name: Thermal equilibrium formula
nodes.statement_short: Under equilibrium boundary data, $N^{eq}=g(\alpha_N+V^{eq})$, $P^{eq}=g(\alpha_P-V^{eq})$ with $V^{eq}$ solving a nonlinear elliptic problem.

nodes.name: Thermal equilibrium densities
nodes.statement: N^{eq}(x)=g\left(\alpha_{N}+V^{eq}(x)\right), \quad P^{eq}(x)=g\left(\alpha_{P}-V^{eq}(x)\right), \quad x \in \Omega,

nodes.name: Thermal equilibrium potential problem

nodes.statement_short: Defines $H$, the relative energy $\mathcal{E}(t)$ from thermal equilibrium and its dissipation $\mathcal{I}(t)$.

nodes.statement: H(s)=\int_{1}^{s}h(\tau)d\tau, \quad s \geq 0,

nodes.statement: \mathcal{E}(t)&=&\int_{\Omega}\left(\vphantom{\frac{1}{2}}H\left(N(t)\right)-H\left(N^{eq}\right)-h\left(N^{eq}\right)\left(N(t)-N^{eq}\right)+H\left(P(t)\right)-H\left(P^{eq}\right)\right. \nonumber\\ & & \quad \left. -h\left(P^{eq}\right)\left(P(t)-P^{eq}\right) +\frac{1}{2}\left\vert \nabla \left(V(t)-V^{eq}\right)\right\vert^{2}\right)dx,
nodes.label: Econtinusc

nodes.name: Energy dissipation (drift-diffusion)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{I}(t)=-\int_{\Omega}\left(N(t)\left\vert \nabla(h(N(t))-V(t))\right\vert^{2}+P(t)\left\vert \nabla(h(P(t))+V(t))\right\vert^{2}\right)dx.

nodes.statement: 0 \leq \mathcal{E}(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\mathcal{I}(\tau)\,d\tau \leq \mathcal{E}(0).

nodes.name: Equilibrium preservation is crucial for long-time behavior
nodes.statement: Looking at these results, it seems crucial that the numerical flux preserves the thermal equilibrium to obtain the consistency of the approximate solution in the long time asymptotic limit.

nodes.name: Convection-diffusion problem with nonlinear diffusion and Dirichlet-Neumann boundary conditions
nodes.statement_short: Find $u$ solving $\partial_t u-\mathrm{div}(\nabla r(u)-\mathbf{q}u)=0$ with initial data $u_0$, Dirichlet data on $\Gamma^D$ and zero Neumann flux on $\Gamma^N$.

nodes.name: Convection-diffusion equation with nonlinear diffusion
nodes.statement: \partial_{t}u-\text{div}(\nabla r(u)-\mathbf{q}u)=0 \text{ for } (x,t) \in \Omega \times (0,T),
nodes.label: eq

nodes.name: Initial condition
nodes.statement: u(x,0)=u_{0}(x) \text{ for } x \in \Omega.
nodes.label: CI

nodes.name: Dirichlet boundary condition
nodes.statement: u(x,t)=\overline{u}(x,t) \text{ for } (x,t) \in \Gamma^{D} \times (0,T),
nodes.label: BCD

nodes.name: Homogeneous Neumann boundary condition
nodes.statement: \nabla r(u) \cdot \mathbf{n}=0 \text{ on } \Gamma^{N} \times (0,T).
nodes.label: BCN

nodes.name: Analysis restricted to Dirichlet boundary conditions
nodes.statement: We will construct the scheme and perform some numerical experiments in the case of Dirichlet-Neumann boundary conditions. However, for the analysis of the scheme, we will only consider the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions ($\partial\Omega=\Gamma^{D}=\Gamma$).

nodes.name: Hypothesis (H1): domain
nodes.statement: \item[(H1)] $\Omega$ is an open bounded connected subset of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, with $d=1,2$ or $3$,

nodes.name: Hypothesis (H2): Dirichlet data
nodes.statement: \item[(H2)] $\partial\Omega=\Gamma^{D}=\Gamma$, $\overline{u}$ is the trace on $\Gamma \times (0,T)$ of a function, also denoted $\overline{u}$, which is assumed to satisfy $\overline{u} \in H^{1}(\Omega \times (0,T))\cap L^{\infty}(\Omega \times (0,T))$ and $\overline{u} \geq 0\textit{ a.e.}$,

nodes.name: Hypothesis (H3): initial data
nodes.statement: \item[(H3)] $u_{0} \in L^{\infty}(\Omega)$ and $u_{0} \geq 0 \textit{ a.e.}$,

nodes.name: Hypothesis (H4): nonlinearity r
nodes.statement: \item[(H4)] $r \in C^{2}(\mathbb{R})$ is strictly increasing on $]0,+\infty[$, $r(0)=r'(0)=0$, with $r'(s)\geq c_{0}s^{\gamma-1}$,

nodes.name: Hypothesis (H5): velocity field
nodes.statement: \item[(H5)] $\mathbf{q} \in C^{1}(\overline{\Omega},\mathbb{R}^{d})$.

nodes.name: Admissible mesh
nodes.statement: A regular and admissible mesh of $\Omega$ is given by a family $\mathcal{T}$ of control volumes (open and convex polygons in 2-D, polyhedra in 3-D), a family $\mathcal{E}$ of edges in 2-D (faces in 3-D) and a family of points $(x_{K})_{K \in \mathcal{T}}$ which satisfy Definition 5.1 in \cite{Eymard2000}. It implies that the straight line between two neighboring centers of cells $(x_{K},x_{L})$ is orthogonal to the edge $\sigma=K|L$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Definition of the finite volume scheme
nodes.statement_short: Control volumes $\mathcal{T}$, edges $\mathcal{E}$ and centres $x_K$ as in Eymard-Gallouët-Herbin, with $x_Kx_L$ orthogonal to $K|L$.

nodes.name: Interior and boundary edges
nodes.statement: In the set of edges $ \mathcal{E}$, we distinguish the interior edges $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int}$ and the boundary edges $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext}$.

nodes.statement: Because of the Dirichlet-Neumann boundary conditions, we split $\mathcal{E}_{ext}$ into $ \mathcal{E}_{ext}=\mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D} \cup \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{N}$ where $ \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D}$ is the set of Dirichlet boundary edges and $ \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{N}$ is the set of Neumann boundary edges.

nodes.name: Edges of a control volume
nodes.statement: For a control volume $K \in \mathcal{T}$, we denote by $\mathcal{E}_{K}$ the set of its edges, $\mathcal{E}_{int,K}$ the set of its interior edges, $\mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}$ the set of edges of $K$ included in $\Gamma^{D}$ and $\mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{N}$ the set of edges of $K$ included in $\Gamma^{N}$.

nodes.name: Classical upwind flux
nodes.statement_short: Two-point flux for $r(u)$ plus upwinded convection $q^+U_K-q^-U_L$.

nodes.name: Classical upwind flux
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \left\{\begin{array}{lll} \tau_{\sigma} \left(r\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)-r\left(U_{L}^{n+1}\right)+d_{\sigma}\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{L}^{n+1}\right)\right), & & \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K},\\ \tau_{\sigma} \left(r\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)-r\left(U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)+d_{\sigma}\left(q_{K,\sigma}^{+}U_{K}^{n+1}-q_{K,\sigma}^{-}U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)\right),& & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D},\\ 0, & & \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{N}, \end{array}\right.
nodes.label: upwindclass

nodes.name: Upwind flux with nonlinear discretization of the diffusion term
nodes.statement_short: Diffusion discretized as $\min(U_K,U_L)\,Dh(U)$ with upwinded convection; also defines the difference operator $Df(U)_{K,\sigma}$.

nodes.name: Nonlinear upwind flux preserves thermal equilibrium
nodes.statement: This flux preserves the thermal equilibrium and it is proved that the numerical solution converges to this equilibrium when time goes to infinity.
conclusions: This flux preserves the thermal equilibrium
the numerical solution converges to this equilibrium when time goes to infinity

nodes.name: Scharfetter-Gummel flux preserves steady-state and is second order
nodes.statement: The Scharfetter-Gummel flux preserves steady-state, and is second order accurate in space (see \cite{Lazarov1996}).
conclusions: The Scharfetter-Gummel flux preserves steady-state
is second order accurate in space

nodes.name: Scharfetter-Gummel flux
nodes.statement_short: $\tau_\sigma(B(-d_\sigma q)U_K-B(d_\sigma q)U_L)$ with the Bernoulli function $B(x)=x/(e^x-1)$.

nodes.name: Scharfetter-Gummel flux with viscosity coefficient
Scharfetter-Gummel flux with viscosity
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}= \tau_{\sigma} \varepsilon \left(B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{\varepsilon}\right)U_{K}^{n+1}-B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{\varepsilon}\right)U_{L}^{n+1}\right) \quad \forall \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}.

nodes.name: Vanishing viscosity limit of the Scharfetter-Gummel flux
conclusions: this flux degenerates into the classical upwind flux for the transport equation $\partial_{t}u-\text{div}(\textbf{q}u)=0$
nodes.statement_short: As $\varepsilon\to0$ the Scharfetter-Gummel flux tends to the upwind flux for pure transport.

nodes.name: The extended flux vanishes at a type of steady-state
nodes.statement: Let $K \in \mathcal{T}$ and $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}$. We assume that $dr_{K,\sigma}$ is defined by (\ref{dr2}) in (\ref{sgext}) and that $U_{K}>0$ and $U_{\sigma}>0$. If $d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}=Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}$, then $\mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}=0$.\\ Indeed, \begin{eqnarray*} \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma} & = & \tau_{\sigma}dr_{K,\sigma}\left(B\left(-\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{K}-B\left(\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}\right)U_{\sigma}\right)\\ &=& \tau_{\sigma}Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}\left(\frac{\exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)U_{K}-U_{\sigma}}{\exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)-1}\right). \end{eqnarray*} But using the definition (\ref{defdr}) of $dr$, we obtain \begin{equation*} \exp\left(\displaystyle{\frac{Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}}{dr_{K,\sigma}}}\right)=\frac{U_{\sigma}}{U_{K}}, \end{equation*} and then $ \mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}=0$. Thus the scheme preserves this type of steady-state.
nodes.statement_short: If $d_\sigma q_{K,\sigma}=Dh(U)_{K,\sigma}$ with positive values then the extended flux vanishes, so this steady-state is preserved.

nodes.name: Proof of the mean value property of dr
nodes.statement: The result is clear if $ab=0$ or $a=b$. Let us suppose that $ab>0$ and $a < b$ (the proof is the same if $a>b$). If we consider the change of variables $x=\log(a)$ and $y=\log(b)$, we obtain \begin{equation*} dr(a,b)=\frac{h(\exp(y))-h(\exp(x))}{y-x} \end{equation*} and using Taylor's formula, there exists $\theta \in [x,y]$ such that \begin{equation*} dr(a,b)=\exp(\theta)h'(\exp(\theta))=r'(\exp(\theta)) \text{ (using the definition of $h$). } \end{equation*} Finally, there exists $\eta=\exp(\theta) \in [a,b]$ such that \begin{equation*} dr(a,b)=r'(\eta). \end{equation*}

The second term is consistent with the diffusive part of equation (\ref{eq}), since $\displaystyle{\coth(x)\underset{0}{\sim}\frac{1}{x}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of well-posedness and L-infinity bounds
nodes.statement: At each time step, the scheme (\ref{CId})-(\ref{BCd})-(\ref{schemegene})-(\ref{flux}) leads to a system of card$(\mathcal{T})$ linear equations on $U^{n+1}=(U^{n+1}_{K})_{K \in \mathcal{T}}$ which can be written: \begin{equation*} A^{n}U^{n+1}=S^{n}, \end{equation*} where : \begin{itemize} \item[$\bullet$] $A^{n}$ is the matrix defined by \begin{alignat*}{3} &A^{n}_{K,K} & = & \frac{\text{m}(K)}{\Delta t}+\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(\frac{-d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right) \,\ \forall K \in \mathcal{T},\\ &A^{n}_{K,L} & = & -\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right) \,\ \forall L \in \mathcal{T} \text{ such that } \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}; \end{alignat*} \item[$\bullet$] $\displaystyle{S^{n}=\left(\frac{\text{m}(K)}{\Delta t}U^{n}_{K}\right)_{K \in \mathcal{T}}+Tb^{n}}$, with \begin{equation*} Tb^{n}_{K} = \left\{\begin{array}{ll} 0 & \text{ if } K \in \mathcal{T} \text{ such that } \text{m}(\partial K\cap \Gamma)=0,\\ \displaystyle{\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(\displaystyle{\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}}\right)U^{n+1}_{\sigma}} & \text{ if } K \in \mathcal{T} \text{ such that } \text{m}(\partial K\cap \Gamma)\neq 0. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} \end{itemize} The diagonal terms of $A^{n}$ are positive and the offdiagonal terms are nonnegative (since $B(x)>0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $dr^{n}_{K,\sigma} \geq 0$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, for all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}$). Moreover, since $dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}=dr_{L,\sigma}^{n}$ and $q_{K,\sigma}=-q_{L,\sigma}$ for all $ \sigma=K|L \in \mathcal{E}_{int}$, we have for all $L \in \mathcal{T}$: \begin{equation*} \left|A^{n}_{L,L}\right|-\sum_{\substack{K \in \mathcal{T} \\ K \neq L}}\left|A^{n}_{K,L}\right|=\frac{\text{m}(L)}{\Delta t}>0, \end{equation*} and then $A^{n}$ is strictly diagonally dominant with respect to the columns. $A^{n}$ is then an M-matrix so $A^{n}$ is invertible, which gives existence and uniqueness of the solution of the scheme. Moreover, $(A^{n})^{-1}\geq 0$ and since $U_{K}^{0} \geq 0$ for all $K\in \mathcal{T}$ (using (H3)) and $U^{n+1}_{\sigma} \geq 0$ for all $n \geq 0$, for all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D}$ (using (H2)), it is easy to prove by induction that $U^{n}_{K} \geq 0$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, for all $n \geq 0$.\\ Now, we suppose that (H6) and (H7) are fulfilled. We prove that $U^{n}_{K}\leq M $ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, for all $n \geq 0$ by induction. Thanks to hypothesis (H7), we have clearly $U^{0}_{K}\leq M $ for all $ K \in \mathcal{T}$.\\ Let us suppose that $U^{n}_{K}\leq M \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}$. We want to prove $U^{n+1}_{K}\leq M \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}$.\\ Let us define $\textbf{M}=(M,...,M)^{T} \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{card}(\mathcal{T})}$. Since $A^{n}$ is an M-matrix, we have $(A^{n})^{-1} \geq 0$ and then it suffices to prove that $A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right) \leq 0$. \\ We first compute $A^{n}\textbf{M}$. Using the following property of the Bernoulli function: \begin{equation} B(x)-B(-x)=-x \quad \forall x \in \mathbb{R}, \end{equation} we obtain that for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, \begin{equation*} \left(A^{n}\textbf{M}\right)_{K}=M\left(\frac{\text{m}(K)}{\Delta t}+\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}+\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(-\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\right). \end{equation*} Then we compute $A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right)$: for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$ \begin{eqnarray*} \left(A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right)\right)_{K} &=& \frac{\text{m}(K)}{\Delta t}(U^{n}_{K}-M)+ \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)U^{n+1}_{\sigma} \\ & & -M \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}-M\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\tau_{\sigma}dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}B\left(-\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right). \end{eqnarray*} By induction hypothesis, the first term is nonpositive. Moreover, using hypothesis (H7) and the property (\ref{propriB}), we obtain \begin{eqnarray*} \left(A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right)\right)_{K} &\leq &-M \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int,K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma} -M \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}\\ &\leq & -M \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}. \end{eqnarray*} However, using hypothesis (H6) and the definition of $q_{K,\sigma}$ (\ref{q}), we get \begin{equation*} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}}\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}=\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}}\int_{\sigma}q \cdot \mathbf{n}_{K,\sigma}\, ds= \int_{K}\text{div}(q)=0, \end{equation*} and then $\left(A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right)\right)_{K} \leq 0$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$.\\ So we have $A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right) \leq 0$, therefore we deduce that $U^{n+1}-\textbf{M} \leq 0$, hence $U^{n+1}_{K} \leq M \quad \forall K$ and we can show by the same way that $U^{n+1}_{K} \geq m \quad \forall K$.
nodes.statement_short: M-matrix argument: the scheme matrix is column diagonally dominant with nonpositive off-diagonals, so it is invertible with nonnegative inverse. Bounds follow by induction, showing $A^n(U^{n+1}-\mathbf{M})\le0$ via $B(x)-B(-x)=-x$ and $\mathrm{div}\,\mathbf{q}=0$.

nodes.name: Proof of the discrete L2(0,T;H1) estimate
nodes.statement: We follow the proof of Lemma 4.2 in \cite{Eymard2006}. Throughout this proof, $D_{i}$ denotes constants which depend only on $r$, $\textbf{q}$, $u_{0}$, $\overline{u}$, $\Omega$ and $T$. We set \begin{equation*} \overline{U}^{n+1}_{K}=\displaystyle{\frac{1}{\Delta t\text{m}(K)}\int_{t^{n}}^{t^{n+1}}\int_{K}\overline{u}(x,t)\, dx \, dt},\, \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \,\ \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} w^{n+1}_{K}=U^{n+1}_{K}-\overline{U}^{n+1}_{K},\, \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \,\ \forall n \in \mathbb{N}. \end{equation*} We multiply the scheme (\ref{schemegene}) by $\Delta t w^{n+1}_{K}$ and we sum over $n$ and $K$. We obtain $A+B=0$, where: \begin{eqnarray*} A &=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}}\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}}\text{m}(K)\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U^{n}_{K}\right)w_{K}^{n+1},\\ B &=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}w^{n+1}_{K}. \end{eqnarray*} \textbf{Estimate of $A$.} This term is treated in \cite{Eymard2006}. We get: \begin{equation} A \geq -\frac{1}{2}\Vert u_{0}-\overline{u}(.,0)\Vert_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2}-2\Vert \partial_{t}\overline{u}\Vert_{L^{1}(\Omega \times (0,T))}|M-m| =-D_{2}. \end{equation} \textbf{Estimate of $B$.} A discrete integration by parts yields (using that $w_{\sigma}^{n+1}=0$ for all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D}$ and for all $n \geq 0$): \begin{equation*} B = \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(w^{n+1}_{K}-w_{L}^{n+1}\right) + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma} \left(w^{n+1}_{K}-w_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right), \end{equation*} which delivers $B=B'-\overline{B}$, with: \begin{eqnarray*} B' &=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U_{L}^{n+1}\right) + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right),\\ \overline{B} &=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(\overline{U}^{n+1}_{K}-\overline{U}_{L}^{n+1}\right) + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(\overline{U}^{n+1}_{K}-\overline{U}_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right). \end{eqnarray*} \textbf{Estimate of $\overline{B}$.} Using the expression (\ref{flux2}) of $\mathcal{F}_{K,\sigma}^{n+1}$, we have $\overline{B}=\overline{B}_{1}+\overline{B}_{2}$ with \begin{eqnarray*} \overline{B}_{1}&=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(U_{K}^{n+1}+U_{L}^{n+1}\right)\left(\overline{U}_{K}^{n+1}-\overline{U}_{L}^{n+1}\right) \\ & & + \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext,K}^{D}}\frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(U_{K}^{n+1}+U_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right)\left(\overline{U}_{K}^{n+1}-\overline{U}_{\sigma}^{n+1}\right),\\ \overline{B}_{2}&=& \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\coth\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\left(U_{K}^{n+1}-U_{L}^{n+1}\right)\left(\overline{U}_{K}^{n+1}-\overline{U}_{L}^{n+1}\right)\\ \end{eqnarray*} The term $\overline{B}_{1}$ is treated like in \cite{Eymard2006}, which leads to \begin{equation*} \vert \overline{B}_{1} \vert \leq M \Vert \textbf{q} \Vert_{\infty}\Vert \overline{u}_{\delta} \Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}\text{dm}(\Omega)=D_{3}. \end{equation*} We apply Young's inequality for $\overline{B}_{2}$: for any $\alpha>0$, we have \begin{eqnarray*} \left\vert \overline{B}_{2} \right\vert &\leq &\frac{\alpha}{2} \sum_{n=0}^{N_{T}} \Delta t \sum_{\substack{\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{int} \\ \sigma=K|L}} \tau_{\sigma}\left(dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}\right)^{2}\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr_{K,\sigma}^{n}}\coth\left(\frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}}\right)\right)^{2}\left(U_{K}^{n+1}-U_{L}^{n+1}\right)^{2}\\ \frac{1}{2\alpha}\Vert \overline{u}_{\delta}\Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2}. \end{eqnarray*} By the hypothesis (H4), we have $\displaystyle{\inf_{s \in [m,M]}r'(s)>0}$. Then, using Lemma \ref{propdr}, the $L^{\infty}$ estimate on $u_{\delta}$ (\ref{estimlinf}) and the hypothesis (H5), we have \begin{equation*} \frac{d_{\sigma}q_{K,\sigma}}{2dr^{n}_{K,\sigma}} \leq \frac{\Vert \textbf{q} \Vert_{\infty}\text{diam}(\Omega)}{\displaystyle{\inf_{s\in [m,M]}r'(s)}}, \, \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\, \forall K \in \mathcal{T}, \, \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}. \end{equation*} Moreover, since $x \mapsto x \coth(x)$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$, we obtain \begin{equation*} \mathcal{T}, \, \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{K}. \end{equation*} Thus we can bound $ \overline{B}$: \begin{equation} \left\vert \overline{B} \right\vert \leq D_{3}+\frac{\alpha}{2}D_{4}\left(\sup_{s \in [m,M]}r'(s)\right)^{2}\Vert u_{\delta} \Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}^{2}+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\Vert \overline{u}_{\delta} \Vert_{1,\mathcal{D}}. \end{equation} \mathcal{E}_{int,K}$ \begin{eqnarray*} \mathcal{F}^{n+1}_{K,\sigma}\left(U^{n+1}_{K}-U^{n+1}_{L}\right) &=& \frac{\text{m}(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}}{2}\left(\left(U_{K}^{n+1}\right)^{2}-\left(U^{n+1}_{L}\right)^{2}\right)\\ & & + \tau_{\sigma} nodes.statement: The following Lemma is a classical consequence of Proposition \ref{propestiml2} and estimates of time translation for $u_{\delta}$ obtained from the scheme (\ref{CId})-(\ref{BCd})-(\ref{schemegene})-(\ref{flux}). The proof is similar to those of Lemma 4.3 and Lemma 4.7 in \cite{Eymard2000}.

Let $u_{\delta}$ be defined by the scheme (\ref{CId})-(\ref{BCd})-(\ref{schemegene})-(\ref{flux}) and by (\ref{defiuapp}).\\ Let $ \hat{u}$ be defined by $\hat{u}_{\delta}=u_{\delta} \text{ a.e. on } \Omega \times (0,T)$ and $\hat{u}_{\delta}=0 \text{ a.e. on } \mathbb{R}^{d+1} \setminus \Omega \times (0,T)$.\\ Then we get the existence of $M_{2}>0$, only depending on $ \Omega$, $T$, $r$, $q$, $u_{0}$, $\overline{u}$ and not on $ \mathcal{D}$ such that \begin{equation} \int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\left(\hat{u}_{\delta}(x+\eta,t)-\hat{u}_{\delta}(x,t)\right)^{2}\, dx\, dt \leq M_{2}|\eta|(|\eta|+4\delta), \quad \forall \eta \in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\left(\hat{u}_{\delta}(x,t+\tau)-\hat{u}_{\delta}(x,t)\right)^{2}\, dx \, dt \leq M_{2}|\tau|, \quad \forall \tau \in \mathbb{R}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Experimental order of convergence of the SG extended scheme
nodes.statement: In Tables \ref{tableconvergenceinf} and \ref{tableconvergence2}, we compare the order of convergence in $L^{\infty}$ and $L^{2}$ norms of the scheme (\ref{CId})-(\ref{BCd})-(\ref{schemegene}) defined on one hand with the classical upwind flux (\ref{upwindclass}) and on the other hand with the Scharfetter-Gummel extended flux (\ref{flux}). We obtain the same order of convergence as in \cite{Eymard2006}. Moreover, it appears that even if we are in a degenerate case, the Scharfetter-Gummel extended scheme is more accurate than the classical upwind scheme.
conclusions: We obtain the same order of convergence as in \cite{Eymard2006}.
even if we are in a degenerate case, the Scharfetter-Gummel extended scheme is more accurate than the classical upwind scheme
nodes.statement_short: Numerically the SG extended scheme is first order in $L^\infty$, about 1.5 in $L^2$, and more accurate than upwind even when degenerate.

nodes.name: PN-junction test case
nodes.statement:
We present a test case for a geometry corresponding to a PN-junction in 2D  picked in the paper of C. Chainais-Hillairet and F. Filbet \cite{Chainais-Hillairet2007}. The doping profile is piecewise constant, equal to $+1$ in the N-region and $-1$ in the P-region.\\
The Dirichlet boundary conditions are
\begin{eqnarray*}
\overline{N}=0.1, \,\ \overline{P}=0.9, \,\ \overline{V}=\frac{h(\overline{N})-h(\overline{P})}{2} & & \text{ on } \{y=1, \,\ 0 \leq x \leq 0.25\},\\
\overline{N}=0.9, \,\ \overline{P}=0.1, \,\ \overline{V}=\frac{h(\overline{N})-h(\overline{P})}{2} & & \text{ on } \{y=0\}.
\end{eqnarray*}
Elsewhere, we put homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions.\\
The pressure is nonlinear: $r(s)=s^{\gamma}$ with $\gamma=5/3$, which corresponds to the isentropic model.\\
We compute the numerical approximation of the thermal equilibrium and of the transient drift-diffusion system on a mesh made of 896 triangles, with time step $\Delta t=0.01$.
nodes.statement_short: 2-D PN-junction with piecewise constant doping, isentropic pressure $r(s)=s^{5/3}$, 896 triangles, $\Delta t=0.01$.

nodes.name: Only the SG-ext scheme avoids saturation (drift-diffusion)
nodes.statement: With the third scheme, we observe that $\mathcal{E}^{n}$ and $\mathcal{I}^{n}$ converge to zero when time goes to infinity, without a saturation phenomenon. This scheme is the only one of the three which preserves thermal equilibrium, so it appears that this property is crucial to have a good asymptotic behavior.
conclusions: $\mathcal{E}^{n}$ and $\mathcal{I}^{n}$ converge to zero when time goes to infinity, without a saturation phenomenon

nodes.name: Reduce to 0<a<b; log change of variables and Taylor
nodes.statement_short: Dispose of trivial cases, assume $0<a<b$, write $dr$ as a difference quotient of $h\circ\exp$ and apply Taylor's formula.

nodes.name: Linear system form
nodes.statement_short: Each time step is a linear system $A^nU^{n+1}=S^n$.

nodes.name: Matrix and right-hand side
nodes.statement_short: Define the entries of $A^n$ and the source $S^n$.

nodes.name: Sign pattern and column diagonal dominance
nodes.statement_short: Positive diagonal, sign-definite off-diagonals and strict column diagonal dominance.

nodes.name: M-matrix gives existence and uniqueness
nodes.statement: $A^{n}$ is then an M-matrix so $A^{n}$ is invertible, which gives existence and uniqueness of the solution of the scheme.
nodes.statement_short: $A^n$ is an M-matrix, hence invertible.

nodes.name: Nonnegativity by induction
nodes.statement: Moreover, $(A^{n})^{-1}\geq 0$ and since $U_{K}^{0} \geq 0$ for all $K\in \mathcal{T}$ (using (H3)) and $U^{n+1}_{\sigma} \geq 0$ for all $n \geq 0$, for all $\sigma \in \mathcal{E}_{ext}^{D}$ (using (H2)), it is easy to prove by induction that $U^{n}_{K} \geq 0$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, for all $n \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegative inverse and nonnegative data give $U^n_K\ge0$ by induction.

nodes.name: Upper bound: base case
nodes.statement: Now, we suppose that (H6) and (H7) are fulfilled. We prove that $U^{n}_{K}\leq M $ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}$, for all $n \geq 0$ by induction. Thanks to hypothesis (H7), we have clearly $U^{0}_{K}\leq M $ for all $ K \in \mathcal{T}$.
nodes.statement_short: Under (H6)-(H7), start the induction for $U^n_K\le M$ at $n=0$.

nodes.name: Induction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Let us suppose that $U^{n}_{K}\leq M \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}$. We want to prove $U^{n+1}_{K}\leq M \quad \forall K \in \mathcal{T}$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the bound at step $n$, aim for $n+1$.

nodes.name: Reduction to a sign condition
nodes.statement: Let us define $\textbf{M}=(M,...,M)^{T} \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{card}(\mathcal{T})}$. Since $A^{n}$ is an M-matrix, we have $(A^{n})^{-1} \geq 0$ and then it suffices to prove that $A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right) \leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: By $(A^n)^{-1}\ge0$ it suffices to show $A^n(U^{n+1}-\mathbf{M})\le0$.

nodes.name: Compute A^n M
nodes.statement_short: Use $B(x)-B(-x)=-x$ to compute $A^n\mathbf{M}$.

nodes.name: Compute A^n(U^{n+1}-M)
nodes.statement_short: Expand $A^n(U^{n+1}-\mathbf{M})$ componentwise.

nodes.name: Bound using induction hypothesis and (H7)
nodes.statement_short: Bound the expression by $-M\sum_\sigma m(\sigma)q_{K,\sigma}$.

nodes.name: Divergence-free flux sum vanishes
nodes.statement_short: Divergence theorem with $\mathrm{div}\,\mathbf{q}=0$ makes the sum vanish.

nodes.name: Conclude upper and lower bounds
nodes.statement: So we have $A^{n}\left(U^{n+1}-\textbf{M}\right) \leq 0$, therefore we deduce that $U^{n+1}-\textbf{M} \leq 0$, hence $U^{n+1}_{K} \leq M \quad \forall K$ and we can show by the same way that $U^{n+1}_{K} \geq m \quad \forall K$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity yields $U^{n+1}\le M$; the lower bound $m$ is analogous.

nodes.name: Setup of the energy method
nodes.statement_short: Test the scheme with $w=U-\overline{U}$ and split into $A+B=0$.

nodes.name: Follow Eymard-Fuhrmann-Gärtner
nodes.statement: We follow the proof of Lemma 4.2 in \cite{Eymard2006}.
nodes.statement_short: The argument follows Lemma 4.2 of Eymard-Fuhrmann-Gärtner.

nodes.name: Constants and discrete boundary lift
nodes.statement_short: Introduce constants $D_i$, averaged boundary data $\overline{U}$ and $w=U-\overline{U}$.

nodes.name: Test the scheme
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by $\Delta t\,w^{n+1}_K$ and sum to get $A+B=0$.

nodes.statement_short: Cite Eymard-Fuhrmann-Gärtner for $A\ge -D_2$.

\end{eqnarray*}

nodes.statement_short: State the four convergences still to prove.

nodes.name: Estimate of B21-B210
nodes.statement_short: Consistency of the two-point gradient on orthogonal meshes plus the $L^2(H^1)$ bound.

nodes.name: Write the difference
nodes.statement_short: Express $B_{21}-B_{210}$ as a gradient consistency error.

nodes.name: Consistency of difference quotient
nodes.statement_short: Orthogonality gives $(\psi_L-\psi_K)/d_\sigma=\nabla\psi\cdot\mathbf{n}+O(\delta)$.

nodes.name: Mean value bound
nodes.statement_short: Average over $T_{K,\sigma}$ and bound by $D_6\delta\Delta t$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and conclude
nodes.statement_short: Mesh regularity, Cauchy-Schwarz and the $L^2(H^1)$ estimate give convergence to 0.

nodes.name: Estimate of B22
nodes.statement_short: $x\coth x-1$ is Lipschitz and vanishes at 0, giving an $O(\delta)$ bound.

nodes.name: Estimate of B23
nodes.statement_short: Lemma on $dr$ and (H4) bound $|dr-r'(U_K)|$ by jumps; conclude with the $L^2(H^1)$ estimate.

nodes.name: Estimate of B220
nodes.statement_short: Same estimate as for $B_{23}$.

nodes.name: Estimate of B3-B30
nodes.statement_short: Split convective terms and show each discrepancy is $O(\delta)$.

nodes.name: Split B3
nodes.statement_short: $B_3=B_{31}+B_{32}$ after integration by parts.

nodes.name: Split B30
Claim: remaining convective terms vanish
Regularity of q
nodes.statement_short: Edge vs dual-cell averages of $\mathbf{q}\cdot\mathbf{n}$ differ by $O(\delta)$.

nodes.name: Bound B32-B320
nodes.statement_short: Bound $B_{32}-B_{320}$ by $O(\delta)$.

nodes.name: Bound B31
nodes.statement_short: Bound $B_{31}$ by $O(\delta)$.

nodes.name: B310 vanishes likewise
nodes.statement: We obtain in the same way that $B_{310}(\delta) \longrightarrow 0$ as $\delta \rightarrow 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument for $B_{310}$.

nodes.name: Weak formulation holds
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the limit: $u$ satisfies the weak formulation, rewritten with $\nabla r(u)$.

nodes.name: Boundary condition
nodes.statement: It remains to show that $u-\overline{u} \in L^{\infty}(0,T;H^{1}_{0}(\Omega))$. This proof is based on the $L^{2}(0,T;H^{1}(\Omega))$ estimate (\ref{estiml2}) and is similar to the one of Theorem 5.1 in \cite{Chainais-Hillairet2003}.
nodes.statement_short: Boundary condition follows from the $L^2(H^1)$ estimate as in Chainais-Hillairet et al.
